s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cyanosis in a young calf with severe cardiac anomalies
salient_findings: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
key_facts: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cyanosis in a young calf with severe cardiac anomalies
salient_findings: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
key_facts: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur

Superior Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
Inferior Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect

Anomalous Origin of the Left Coronary Artery from the Right Pulmonary Artery
per_call: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
Superior Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
Inferior Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
Anomalous Left Coronary Artery from the Pulmonary Artery
Anomalous Origin of the Left Coronary Artery from the Right Pulmonary Artery

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

shortlist.label: Tricuspid Atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at septal defects

shortlist.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice

shortlist.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
shortlist.why_kept: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and harsh bronchovesicular lung sounds

shortlist.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial dilation

raw.rationale: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and bidirectional shunting at septal defects support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Atresia
rejected.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation suggests the tricuspid valve is not atretic.

rejected.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
rejected.why: While the left ventricle is hypoplastic, the primary issue is the double outlet from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a ventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, and an overriding aorta, which does not fully match the described defects.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: Characterized by an abnormal tricuspid valve and right ventricular hypoplasia, which is not the primary issue in this case.
